missions.title: The Customer Ticket That Crossed Tenants
missions.objective: Identify the true authorization boundary and propose testable containment, correction and release criteria for cross-tenant data exposure.

brief.customer: A fictional multi-tenant AI support product serves multiple business customers. A user at tenant A saw a support ticket belonging to tenant B. A launch is scheduled for tomorrow.
brief.system: Browser -> API -> retrieval service -> shared ticket index -> LLM response. The browser supplies a tenantId parameter; an API route accepts it without an authorization check in one read path.
brief.stakes: Customers' confidential tickets may be exposed; business pressure favors shipping quickly.
constraints: No access to the actual production environment
Use fictional systems and evidence only
A rollout decision must account for uncertain blast radius

phases.coachQuestion: What would you do first, would you proceed with tomorrow's launch, and which assumption matters most?
Where is authorization actually enforced, and what evidence would distinguish a UI filtering issue from a server-side access control defect?
Your AI teammate says the fix is ready. What would you challenge before approving it?

simulatedTeammate.label: FICTIONAL AI CODING AGENT — NOT ACTUAL TOOL OUTPUT
simulatedTeammate.proposal: I added a tenantId filter to the frontend ticket list and all 24 existing unit tests pass. We can deploy and launch tomorrow.
knownLimitations: The API still trusts caller-supplied tenant IDs
Existing tests do not cover cross-tenant resource IDs

inject.label: FICTIONAL NEW CONSTRAINT
inject.text: Security reports a second read path used by exports. Marketing wants to launch anyway. The on-call engineer has 30 minutes before handoff.

phases.coachQuestion: Specify the minimum server-side checks, cross-tenant regression tests, and monitoring needed before declaring the incident contained.
Work independently on the new scenario. State your decision, why, and the verification evidence. No hints are available for this attempt.

anchors: Does not identify user impact or the cross-tenant risk
Mentions risk but lacks evidence/containment plan
Prioritizes containment, blast radius and independently verifiable impact
Relies on client filtering or untrusted tenant field

Binds verified identity to tenant authorization at every read/export/mutation boundary
Accepts passing tests and agent claim uncritically
Questions the agent but lacks adversarial evidence
Defines why 24 tests are insufficient and requests cross-tenant negative tests
Offers no reproducible failure or regression test
Defines deterministic tenant A/B denial tests, logs and a release gate
Adjusts containment/release decision, prioritizes export path and communicates risk
Communicates evidence, uncertainty, stop/rollback criteria and ownership

criticalErrors: Treats client-side tenant filters as authorization
Claims an unverified patch ensures no cross-tenant leakage
Recommends launching without addressing known cross-tenant exposure

suggestedNextTask.task: Write a negative authorization test for the fictional ticket API and export endpoint.
suggestedNextTask.definitionOfDone: A valid tenant-A identity cannot read/export tenant-B resources even when the resource ID and tenantId are known.

transferVariants.brief: A fictional document-sharing SaaS exposes a download API. An AI agent proposes hiding cross-organization documents from search results after a user downloads another organization's file by guessing its ID. The export endpoint remains unchanged. Decide whether the fix is sufficient and how to prove isolation.
transferVariants.prompt: Without hints, identify the authorization boundary, your immediate containment/release decision, and two negative tests that would prove tenant isolation.
excludedHints: Do not reveal the parent mission's authorization rule, rubric anchors or passing answer before submission.
Do not include model-generated suggestions during the unassisted attempt.

requiredAssertions: Server authorizes verified identity and resource organization relationship
Search filtering cannot replace download/export authorization
criticalErrors: Accepts UI-only document hiding as sufficient
Claims guessed IDs are safe because unlikely
